To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
caffeine chelates Ca2+ in the lumen (and matrix) of the endoplamic reticulum (and mitochondria) and this effect can be modulated by ryanodine receptors.
caffeine chelates calcium from the lumen of both the endoplasmatic reticulum and mitochondria, but not from the cytoplasm.

(1) Caffeine chelated Ca2+ in the ER lumen, (2) Caffeine induced Ca2+ release from the ER, (3) Caffeine increased cytosolic Ca levels in RyR3 expressing cells, (4) Caffeine did not chelate cytosolic Ca, and (5) The caffeine induced Ca release was RyR3 dependent.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of caffeine on the Ca2+ concentration inside the ER and the mitochondria.
the action of caffeine on intracellular Ca2+.
the effects of caffeine on Ca2+ homeostasis in the endoplasmatic reticulum (and mitochondria) and the cytosol.

caffeine can be a powerful tool to investigate ER Ca2+ signaling when used at low concentrations, but that its use at high concentrations can lead to misleading interpretations of Ca2+ signaling.
